order_answers.answer: The reading guide establishes three different contributions. Part 1 moves from representation/noise prerequisites to surviving neural displacement and then information/readout. Part 2 applies dynamics to eye evidence before separately building spatial maps. The advertised chapter 1 then 5 path does not require chapter 3 results. This is supported by the reading-guide paths and chapter-plan purposes, not a review of all later chapter prose.

Chapter 1 takes an observable retention problem through spikes, count variability, covariance, attractor geometry and accumulating diffusion. Static spatial randomness then separates the third paper. Chapter 2 starts from the attractor question, constructs recurrent activity, derives the lasting direction, projects noise, simplifies under symmetry and treats time/domain/drift limits before reading paper figures. Each contribution title names the actual addition.

Moving the covariance block immediately before diffusion would make its memory use more immediate, but its present position supplies a compact probability bridge from count variability and also serves the eye branch. Moving the paper map to the beginning would require reading its static-versus-dynamic distinction before it is taught. Retain current order. The covariance heading could optionally mention shared fluctuations because most of its opening prepares that topic; this is a navigation preference, not missing teaching.
